title: Out-of-work musicians, undercutting and hotel jobs
summary: Musicians complained of others working cheaper; he never held a steady hotel job, only gigs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: There's a whole area that I want to - while you were making all this money every week, there were a lot of musicians

who weren't making any money (they were out of work), who could play. I'm sure you knew many of them who were not working. Did you ever hear musicians talk about the things that were wrong, that they felt were wrong, why they weren't working?
What kinds of things were they talking about?
Sometimes they would get together and they'd want to work. One said, 'He's trying to cut my throat,' you know, for a job, working cheaper and all like that. That was true; guys did do that.
Suppose there had been a time here in New York when all the black bands played in all of the hotels here. Is that true?
Suppose there had been a period here in New York in the 30's where all of the hotels downtown hired black bands. Is that so?
Not in the 30's? Like they would work in the Hotel Taft and Biltmore and all that?
Did you never work in any of those hotels?
But you did work them on occasion.
I played gigs, like that, not a steady job.
No, I never worked on a steady job in a hotel.
